title: Bat Talk and Tour
location: Yolo Basin Foundation, Yolo Bypass Wildlife Area
description:
The Bats are Back at the Yolo Causeway in Davis 
  
Summer is here, and the bats are back!  
  
Join Yolo Basin Foundation this summer on a Bat Talk and Tour. Learn about these amazing flying mammals that do so much to help reduce insect pests throughout the area. Live native bat species are displayed as part of the presentation. The program culminates in watching the bats as they emerge from under the freeway. 
  
The maternity Mexican free-tailed bat colony under the I-80 Yolo Causeway is growing daily as they return from wherever they spent the winter. Although many of the bats over-winter in the bridge, most seem to leave. As the weather warms, crops grow and insect populations explode, the bats return to the Causeway.  
  
These amazing, winged wonders are mammals that fly. Each summer the females give birth, in late June, to one pup. She nurses that pup for about 5 to 6 weeks, and then it joins her as she flies throughout the Central Valley to consume crop pests and mosquitos. There also are males that live in the Yolo Causeway bridge. 
  
Throughout the summer, Yolo Basin Foundation offers many opportunities to learn more about the bats. Registration is now open.  
  
Children who are interested in bats are encouraged to join Yolo Basin Foundation for a morning of “Bats and Crafts”.  Meet live bats from our local area then have fun creating crafts and playing bat games. This special event is aimed at young children, especially those that are too young to stay up late to watch the bats fly. 
  
All events and some fun fact videos about our programs and the bats can be found at https://yolobasin.org/battalkandtour/ . 
  
Yolo Basin Foundation offers environmental education programs for all ages related to wetlands and wildlife.

title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:
**We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)

We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.

People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.

Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants and businesses.

Join Yolo Basin Foundation this summer on a Bat Talk and Tour. Learn about these amazing flying mammals that do so much to help reduce insect pests throughout the area. Live native bat species are displayed as part of the presentation. The program culminates in watching the bats as they emerge from under the freeway. 
  
The maternity Mexican free-tailed bat colony under the I-80 Yolo Causeway is growing daily as they return from wherever they spent the winter. Although many of the bats over-winter in the bridge, most seem to leave. As the weather warms, crops grow and insect populations explode, the bats return to the Causeway.  
  
These amazing, winged wonders are mammals that fly. Each summer the females give birth, in late June, to one pup. She nurses that pup for about 5 to 6 weeks, and then it joins her as she flies throughout the Central Valley to consume crop pests and mosquitos. There also are males that live in the Yolo Causeway bridge. 
  
Throughout the summer, Yolo Basin Foundation offers many opportunities to learn more about the bats. Registration is now open.  
  
Children who are interested in bats are encouraged to join Yolo Basin Foundation for a morning of “Bats and Crafts”.  Meet live bats from our local area then have fun creating crafts and playing bat games. This special event is aimed at young children, especially those that are too young to stay up late to watch the bats fly. 
  
All events and some fun fact videos about our programs and the bats can be found at https://yolobasin.org/battalkandtour/ . 
  
Yolo Basin Foundation offers environmental education programs for all ages related to wetlands and wildlife.

title: A Hands-On Collaborative Ceramic Installation
location: International House Davis, 10 College Park, Davis, CA, 95616, United States
description:
Join ceramic artist Pinar Brummer for a hands-on, community-led gathering at International House Davis, in two parts. Together, we’ll shape a collaborative tree sculpture, then slow down to hand-build our own small ceramic pieces. No experience needed, just a willingness to show up, get elemental, and tap into some childlike joy. 
Pinar opens the gathering with her own story, her journey from Türkiye to Davis, and how it inspired this project, before inviting you to get your hands in the clay and be your childlike self. 
Part One: The Tree. Everything you touch, touches you is a reflection on togetherness, on how we’re not just observers but active participants in a shared experience, connected to each other and the world around us. At the heart of the gathering is an incomplete ceramic tree, hand-built by Pinar, waiting for your mark. You’ll shape a clay leaf to join it, no skill required, each one becoming part of a lasting, collective piece. 
Part Two: The Tea Cup. Pinar will guide you through hand-building a small, imperfect tea cup, a slow, meditative practice that celebrates flaws rather than smoothing them away. 
The finished tree will be on display at International House for several weeks, then celebrated at a Reveal Party where you’ll see how everyone’s marks came together into one collective piece. 
Come ready to get your hands dirty and leave a piece of yourself behind. This is a sensory, emotional experience that gets you in touch with your childlike core, and with each other.  Ages 16 and up.

title: Davis Jazz Beat Festival
location: CA
description:
In honor of the incredible legacy of Beat poets, musicians, and artists, the John Natsoulas Gallery will host a two-day event dedicated to the arts that defined a generation in the Bay Area. Join us to experience live music, poetry readings, and performance painting! All events will take place at the John Natsoulas Gallery or across the street at the Davis Commons. 
All ages are welcome and the admission is free!

title: Imagining America National Gathering
location: CA
description:
Join over 500 participants from the IA network and the University of California, Davis and Yolo Bioregion community (a geographic and cultural area that includes the cities of Davis, Woodland, Winters, West Sacramento, and surrounding areas) to engage in deep learning, collaboration, and transformative creativity on the theme of Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times. We will activate spaces across the UC Davis campus, in the City of Davis, and at community-hosted site visits. 
Tides of Transition: Restoring Collective Spirit in Troubled Times calls us to re-story and honor the places, knowledges, relationships, and ecologies that have been made broken through centuries of violence and abandonment, and the current intensifying fear and repression. We know that our communities are tired, and we know that being together revives our collective spirit, giving us the strength and inspiration we need in troubled times. In this moment of upheaval, the 2026 IA National Gathering draws participants to Davis, CA in the spirit of mending the roots of our connections, and to “awaken,” as Buddhist monk and activist Thích Nhất Hạnh teaches, “from the illusion of our separateness.”

title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note
description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering
Update 8/14/25:

title: Dia de los Muertos
location: Davis Cemetery, 820 Pole Line Rd, Davis, CA, 95618, United States
description: On an annual basis, the Davis Cemetery District hosts a Dia de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) celebration on our grounds. This celebration is one of the last Mesoamerican indigenous influenced rituals, honoring mother earth and all ancestors. This celebration is part of an effort to create a community, a sense of belonging, and global awareness of cultural richness in our multicultural society.

description: CommuniCare+OLE hosts an annual, free community Dia de Muertos celebration in Woodland, California, aimed at honoring Mexican heritage and reducing mental health stigma. description:

The first Wednesday of every month, we play _Blood on the Clocktower_, a social deduction game in the vein of Werewolf/Mafia/The Resistance, with a few twists!

title: Walnut Park Library Grand Opening
location: Walnut Park Library, 2660 Lilliard Drive, Davis, CA, 95618, United States
description: The Walnut Park Library Grand Opening and Ribbon-Cutting Ceremony will take place on Saturday, November 7, 2026, at 9:00 AM at 2660 Lillard Drive in South Davis. Sponsored by the Friends of the Davis Public Library, this all-ages community event marks the official opening of Yolo County’s newest 12,000+ square-foot facility. title: International Festival Davis
location: International House Davis, 10 College Park, Davis, 95616, United States
description:
Join us on November 7 at International House Davis for I-Fest 2026, our International Festival Davis! 
For one day, we open our doors wide to celebrate and uplift the many cultures and people who make our region so vibrant. Explore cultural and artisan booths throughout I-House, enjoy food trucks out front, and experience a full lineup of performances on our backyard stage. It’s an open house in the truest sense: for the day, this is your house too, and every culture and community has a place here. 
I-Fest is a celebration, but your participation also supports the work I-House does all year long: welcoming newcomers, supporting English learners, and helping people from around the world find connection and community in Davis. At a time when many of us are feeling anxious or disconnected, creating spaces for joy, belonging, and connection feels more important than ever. Come celebrate cultures, meet new people, share in the joy, and experience what makes our community so special. 
For one day, I-House is your house. Come be part of it.

title: Principles of Community Celebration
location: UC Davis ARC, 760 Orchard Road, Davis, CA, 95616
description:
The 2026 Principles of Community Celebration recognizes the people and partnerships that bring our values to life across UC Davis.

We honor our collective decision to be part of this community, and we celebrate the ongoing work of making UC Davis a place people want to be. 
For more information, visit: https://excellence.ucdavis.edu/events/principles-community-celebration.
